title: Occupational Needlestick Injury: HIV and Viral Hepatitis Post-Exposure Pathway
specialty: Infectious Diseases / Occupational Health / Emergency Medicine

evidenceAudit.scope: Occupational Needlestick Injury: HIV and Viral Hepatitis Post-Exposure Pathway
findings: Built as an additive Disease Management version using the approved-topic structure.
Investigations are ordered from bedside/laboratory assessment to imaging and specialist tests.
The original outline remains current; this version is non-current and pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: Saudi national occupational PEP regimen and SFDA product availability were not opened.
Exact antiretroviral and hepatitis-B immunoglobulin doses are deferred to the current local formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Percutaneous or mucosal exposure can transmit blood-borne viruses depending on fluid, injury and source status. Human immunodeficiency virus post-exposure prophylaxis works best when started promptly. Hepatitis B management depends on vaccination and antibody response; no hepatitis C prophylactic drug is recommended.
keyMechanisms: Percutaneous or mucosal exposure can transmit blood-borne viruses depending on fluid, injury and source status.
Human immunodeficiency virus post-exposure prophylaxis works best when started promptly.

symptoms: Usually asymptomatic at exposure; later systemic symptoms are non-specific.
physicalSigns: Puncture, cut, splash to mucosa or contact with non-intact skin.
redFlags: Deep injury with a hollow-bore blood-filled needle, known viraemic source, mucosal high-volume exposure or delayed presentation.
precipitants: Sharps injury, unsafe disposal, recapping, splash or procedural exposure.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Intact skin contact with non-blood fluid and no portal of entry.
Requires the non-occupational pathway and safeguarding/risk assessment.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Significant percutaneous, mucosal or non-intact-skin exposure
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Decide immediately whether HIV PEP and hepatitis B prophylaxis are indicated.
ruleIn.normalValue: No infectious-fluid exposure through a portal of entry

clinicalManagement.title: First aid and report
actions: Wash puncture/cut with soap and water; irrigate mucosa with water; do not squeeze or use caustic agents.
Report immediately to occupational health/emergency pathway and document device, fluid, depth and source.

clinicalManagement.title: Start indicated prophylaxis
actions: Begin a recommended three-drug HIV PEP regimen without waiting for all results when exposure is significant.
Apply the hepatitis B vaccine/immunoglobulin pathway according to immunity and source status; no hepatitis C PEP is given.

clinicalManagement.title: Follow and support
actions: Review tolerability, interactions, renal/hepatic factors and adherence.
Complete guideline-timed HIV, HBV and HCV testing and give psychological/occupational support.

medicationPlan.note: Use the 2025 occupational HIV PEP preferred regimen selected by infectious diseases/occupational health for 28 days, adjusted for pregnancy, renal function and interactions. Apply hepatitis B vaccine plus hepatitis B immunoglobulin only according to documented immunity and source status. Exact products and doses require the Saudi occupational-health formulary and SFDA verification.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Blood or infectious fluid contacts percutaneous injury, mucosa or non-intact skin.
Start as soon as possible; do not delay the first dose for source results when indicated.

teaching.scope: Occupational Needlestick Injury: HIV and Viral Hepatitis Post-Exposure Pathway
learningObjectives: Recognise the emergency and relevant red flags.
Select the correct investigation and escalation pathway.
Use medicines only within the stated branch and local formulary.
pitfalls: Delaying specialist escalation while waiting for a non-essential test.
Using an unverified medicine dose or applying an adult pathway to a child.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval.

patientEducation: Explain transmission risk, adherence, adverse effects, safer sex/blood donation precautions and follow-up testing.
lifestyleAndDiet: No work exclusion is usually required solely because PEP is taken; follow occupational-health advice.
mdtReferrals: Occupational health immediately; infectious diseases/HIV specialist for complex exposure or source resistance.
dischargeCriteria: First PEP dose supplied when indicated, baseline samples taken, source plan and follow-up appointment documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Occupational-health follow-up through completion of the current HIV/HBV/HCV testing schedule.
